newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer static despite FTSE surge.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer static despite FTSE surge.

text.p: Shares in Marks & Spencer Plc defied the UK market's sharp gains on Thursday amid concern over the impact of the sale of privately-owned Littlewoods stores and talk of a slowdown in retail sales growth, dealers said.

M&S shares were unchanged at 488p by 1256 GMT and other leading retail stocks were also mixed, with Dixons Group Plc down 5p at 528-1/2, Kingfisher Plc up just 1/2p at 684 and Boots Co Plc unchanged at 668.
By contrast, the FTSE 100 index was up 36.2 points at 4,396.2 after hitting a record 4,396.8.

Analysts at BZW warned that the proposed sale of Littlewoods since it could lead to a relatively weak clothing retailer being replaced by a more effective food retailer in prominent positions close to M&S stores.
Analysts at the brokerage were not immediately available for comment. Food retailers such as Safeway Plc, down 1p at 366, are seen as among the most likely bidders for Littlewoods stores.

Separately a survey from the Confederation of British Industry said UK retail sales growth in the three months to February was the lowest since May 1996, with trading in February not up to shopkeepers expectations.
Analysts said renewed caution by consumers ahead of the election, expected on May 1, could be behind the lacklustre findings.
